content:
amina: FYI — since the kernel/firmware push last night we've been seeing intermittent gRPC stream resets between pods on nodepool-gpu-usw2-a and -b. App logs show lots of ECONNRESET + occasional "EMSGSIZE" errors.

josh: ugh. any correlation with instance reboots or kernel version?

amina: most nodes are on 5.15.0-88 -> 5.15.0-92 (rollout finished ~01:10 UTC). Reboots were during the window. Observed higher packet drop for east-west traffic in cloud provider metrics.

ryan: can you paste the tcpdump or netlog of a failing stream?

amina: attaching snippet (simplified):
```
18:42:13.123 IP pod-a > pod-b: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12890, ack 56789, win 64240, length 545
18:42:13.124 IP pod-a > pod-b: Fragmented packet, original length 1500 > mtu?
18:42:13.125 IP pod-b > pod-a: ICMP frag needed and DF set, length 68, MTU 1400
18:42:13.126 pod-a > pod-b: TCP RST, seq 0, win 0
```

amina: so we see a PMTU ICMP message then RSTs. Pod-to-pod traffic across nodes appears to hit a lower MTU on the path (vxlan + encap + RDMA?)

priya: did the CNI change or did kube-proxy toggle any offload flags? I remember a config tweak to enable GSO/TSO in the CNI last month.

josh: last week we enabled generic-segmentation-offload on the host NICs again for perf. Some providers changed underlying tunnel MTU defaults recently. If GSO is on and path MTU is lower, kernels should be clamped but older kernels sometimes mishandle it leading to ESMGSIZE/ICMP cascades.

ryan: quick tests you can run on a repro node:
- `ip link show` to verify mtu on vxlan/geneve interfaces
- `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` (set 1 temporarily)
- `sudo ethtool -k <iface>` to check gso/gro/tx offloads
- run `ping -M do -s 1400 <other-node>` to force path MTU checks

amina: ran some already: vxlan0 mtu=1450 on node-a, but physical nic is 9000, tunnel overhead 50 -> should be 8950 i guess. But the cloud overlay has intermediate hop limiting to 1400.

priya: that mismatch would explain the ICMP need-to-fragment. If kernel refuses to fragment (DF set), gRPC streaming which uses large messages and streaming windows hits a hard error path and the client tears down.

josh: mitigation options:
- clamp MSS on the bridge/router (prefered)
- disable GSO/TCP segmentation offload on the vxlan interfaces (works but perf regresses)
- enable `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` cluster-wide while we root cause

ryan: also check NIC firmware/rdma drivers. RDMA stack sometimes bypasses normal skb paths and the offload interactions are weird. If any nodes had updated driver version during kernel push, that could be the trigger.

amina: agreed. I'm going to: 1) enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 on a canary nodepool; 2) add an iptables mangle rule to clamp MSS for tcp on vxlan interface; 3) collect `ethtool -k` and `dmesg | grep -i icmp` across nodes.

priya: please include affected pod namespaces and pod names so we can correlate app-level retries/metrics. Also raise a ticket to cloud provider support to confirm any changes to overlay MTU in the region.

infra-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-1084 — "East-West packet MTU mismatch causing streaming resets" (priority P2). Assigned to eng-infra. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2026-1084

amina: thanks — I'll post results of the canary in this thread in ~30m. :hourglass:
